news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor's AI Push Hits Surprising Milestone
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( NYSE:TSM ) may accelerate production of its advanced 3-nanometer chips several months ahead of schedule, giving investors another signal that demand from Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ) and Broadcom remains exceptionally strong. The earlier ramp could support faster second-half revenue growth while easing a critical supply constraint for leading AI-chip designers.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with INTC.

Is TSM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker, manufacturing processors designed by companies that do not operate their own advanced fabrication plants. Its most sophisticated production nodes command premium pricing and are increasingly important for AI accelerators, data-center processors and high-end consumer electronics.

Wedbush said TSMC could reach 180,000 monthly 3-nanometer wafer starts early in the fourth quarter, two to three months earlier than previously expected. That would represent a sizable increase from approximately 150,000 wafer starts per month during the first half of 2026.

The added production is reportedly supported by orders from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, three companies benefiting directly from rising spending on AI computing infrastructure.

TSMC's next-generation 2-nanometer ramp may also be progressing rapidly. Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson said monthly starts could rise from 50,000 to 60,000 during the first half to more than 80,000 early in the fourth quarter and approach 100,000 by year-end.

On 2nm, the paper puts 1H26 starts at 50-60k per month, rising above 80k by early 4Q and approaching 100k by year-end, which would take combined 2nm plus 3nm above 260k per month, Bryson said.

TSMC shares rose 2.5% by midday Tuesday.

Investor Takeaway On TSMC Stock

Investors should watch whether increased wafer starts translate into stronger utilization, revenue and margins rather than simply higher capacity. Sustained orders from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom would support TSMC's upbeat second-half outlook and reinforce its technological lead.

The investment case would strengthen if the 2-nanometer ramp stays on schedule and customers commit to multiyear volumes. The key risks are weaker AI demand, lower manufacturing yields or aggressive capacity additions that pressure pricing. Advanced-node revenue mix and gross-margin guidance will be crucial indicators in TSMC's next earnings update.

news.Title: Sandisk: Solid Q4 Ahead, Yet the Stock Looks Undervalued
news.Content:
Sandisk (SNDK) is scheduled to report its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, Aug. 5. Expectations are high for another strong quarter, supported by sustained AI-driven demand and a favorable pricing environment in the NAND memory market. These factors could enable the company to deliver revenue and earnings above consensus estimates.

Despite these positive fundamentals, SNDK stock has declined about 40% from its recent peak, creating a notable disconnect between its operating performance and market valuation. If the company delivers another strong quarter and provides an upbeat outlook, the current share price could represent an attractive long-term buying opportunity.

More News from Barchart

General Motors vs. Ford: 1 Auto Giant Is Winning the EV Race

Jeff Bezos Says He's Selling $1 Billion In Amazon Stock Every Year to Fund Blue Origin — 'It's The Most Important Work I'm Doing'

1 Japanese Company Just Waved a Red Flag for Micron Stock. How to Play It Here.

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

AI Demand and Pricing Tailwinds Point to Another Strong Quarter

Sandisk expects revenue of $7.75 billion to $8.25 billion in Q4, with the midpoint of $8 billion implying approximately 321% year-over-year (YOY) growth. That would mark acceleration after fiscal Q3 revenue surged 251% YOY to $5.95 billion.

Sandisk's primary growth driver remains the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure. As hyperscalers and enterprises deploy increasingly AI-intensive workloads, demand for high-performance NAND storage continues to rise. This structural shift is driving higher shipment volumes while also supporting stronger pricing across the memory industry.

A favorable supply-demand balance has further strengthened the company's position. Rising NAND prices have boosted both revenue and operating cash flow, and management believes these pricing dynamics are likely to remain favorable through calendar 2026 and beyond. This has encouraged Sandisk to increase investments in higher-value opportunities that can support both near-term growth and long-term profitability.

Another key growth engine is the data-center business. Revenue from this segment is expected to remain robust, benefiting from both higher shipment volumes and improved average selling prices (ASPs).

Overall, accelerating AI-related storage demand and higher ASPs provide confidence in Sandisk's growth trajectory.

Margin Expansion Should Drive an Earnings Beat

Story Continues

Strong revenue growth is expected to translate into significant profitability gains in Q4.

Higher average selling prices, improving product mix, and continued growth in exabyte shipments should support further gross margin expansion. Management has guided for an adjusted gross margin of 79% to 81% in Q4, with the midpoint of 80% representing both a sequential improvement and substantial YOY expansion.

Sandisk expects adjusted EPS between $30 and $33, compared with $0.29 in the year-ago quarter and $23.41 in Q3 2026. Notably, Wall Street expects adjusted EPS of $33.28, which is slightly above guidance. That suggests analysts see additional upside from favorable pricing and operating leverage.

Overall, another quarter of strong execution appears likely, with both revenue and earnings benefiting from durable AI-driven demand and a strong memory pricing cycle.

Valuation Does Not Reflect Sandisk's Growth Potential

Despite the sharp improvement in fundamentals, Sandisk's valuation remains low following the recent selloff. SNDK stock currently trades at just 6.5 times forward earnings, a multiple that appears difficult to justify given the company's earnings trajectory and favorable industry backdrop.

Sandisk is benefiting from one of the strongest AI-related demand cycles in the semiconductor industry. Analyst consensus estimates call for 188% EPS growth in fiscal 2027, even against challenging YOY comparisons. If Sandisk continues to execute as expected, its earnings growth could justify a significantly higher valuation multiple over time.

Another overlooked catalyst is the company's new business models (NBMs), the multiyear supply agreements that improve revenue visibility and reduce earnings volatility. At the time of its Q3 earnings release, Sandisk had signed five agreements, with three agreements signed during the quarter offering a combined minimum revenue commitment of $42 billion. As the memory firm signs additional long-term contracts, visibility into recurring revenue should improve further, strengthening the investment case.

The Bottom Line

Sandisk enters its Q4 earnings report with strong momentum. AI-driven demand, improving NAND pricing, expanding margins, and accelerating data-center growth position the company to deliver another impressive quarter.

Yet SNDK stock looks undervalued. With earnings expected to grow rapidly, long-term supply agreements adding stability, and AI infrastructure spending remaining robust, Sandisk appears well-positioned for further upside. Wall Street is bullish, with most analysts recommending a "Strong Buy" on Sandisk stock.

news.Title: Apple Scores Major Win in One of Its Biggest Markets
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) has reportedly crossed $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time, giving investors fresh evidence that the country is becoming a meaningful growth market and an increasingly important hedge against Apple's exposure to China.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with DELL.

Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Revenue in India rose at a double-digit rate during the 12 months through March, up from about $9 billion a year earlier, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. iPhones generated most of the sales, while demand for iPads and MacBooks also increased.

The milestone remains small relative to Apple's global business, but its strategic importance is considerably larger. India offers Apple a vast smartphone market with rising incomes, expanding premium-device demand and far lower iPhone penetration than mature markets such as the U.S.

Apple is also strengthening its direct relationship with Indian consumers. The company opened another Mumbai store in February, bringing its official retail-store count in the country to six. A larger retail footprint can improve product visibility, financing access, trade-in activity and sales of higher-margin services and accessories.

India is simultaneously becoming central to Apple's supply-chain strategy. Five factories now manufacture iPhones in the country, and roughly one in every four iPhones is reportedly made there. India has also become the main production source for devices shipped to the U.S.

That diversification matters as Apple faces geopolitical uncertainty and tougher competition in China. Its latest quarterly China revenue totaled $18.8 billion, below some analysts' $19.6 billion estimate, as local rivals including Huawei continue to challenge the iPhone.

Investor Takeaway On Apple Stock

Investors should watch whether India's revenue growth remains above Apple's companywide rate and whether the expansion broadens beyond iPhones into Macs, iPads, wearables and services.

Further store openings, stronger premium-smartphone share and increased local production could improve Apple's long-term growth and reduce supply-chain concentration. However, India is unlikely to replace China's revenue contribution soon. Pricing, import rules, local competition and consumer affordability remain key constraints. The strongest signal would be sustained double-digit sales growth alongside rising margins and deeper services adoption.

news.Title: Pinterest expects slower quarterly revenue growth as ad competition heats up
news.Content:
By Jaspreet Singh

Aug 4 (Reuters) - Image-sharing platform Pinterest forecast slower revenue growth for the third quarter on Tuesday, a sign of tough ‌competition for digital advertising from bigger players including Meta's Instagram, sending its ‌shares down 9% in extended trading.

Pinterest has been expanding Performance+, its AI-powered suite for advertisers, ​to attract more marketers by helping them optimize and scale their campaigns with less manual effort.

As Meta continues to improve its Advantage+ ad automation tools, Reddit launched a broadly similar product and with ads becoming a larger focus for OpenAI, competition ‌is expected to increase further.

Last ⁠month, Google revamped Google Images with AI-powered personalized feeds and visual discovery features resembling Pinterest, indicating a broader push for ⁠AI-driven search and shopping by the search-engine giant.

"We faced incremental pressure mid-quarter from Asia-based cross-border retailers impacted by regulatory actions particularly in Europe and that pressure is ​continuing in ​the third quarter," CFO Julia Donnelly said ​on the company's post-earnings call.

Pinterest ‌expects its current-quarter revenue to be in the range of $1.19 billion to $1.21 billion, representing a 13% to 15% growth, compared with analysts' average estimate of $1.20 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

That is slower than the 18% revenue growth in its second quarter. The company reported $1.18 billion in revenue for the three ‌months ended June 30, beating estimates of $1.15 billion.

"Its ​AI tools have shown early promise, but ​they haven't generated the same level ​of enthusiasm as competitors' offerings," said Emarketer analyst Marisa Jones.

Pinterest's ‌global monthly active users rose 11% ​to 640 million ​in the second quarter from a year ago, while average revenue per user rose 7% to $1.86.

Earlier this year, the company completed its acquisition of ​tvScientific, a move aimed ‌at extending advertisers' reach beyond social media and into connected TV ​and giving Pinterest a broader pool of ad budgets.

(Reporting by Jaspreet ​Singh in Bengaluru; Editing by Shreya Biswas)

news.Title: Apollo Global Management Q2 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Apollo Global Management Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Apollo reported record second-quarter results , with fee-related earnings up 25% year over year to $785 million and spread-related earnings reaching $877 million. Adjusted net income totaled $1.3 billion, or $2.11 per share.

Origination and fundraising showed strong momentum: Apollo originated $74 billion during the quarter, recorded a record $60 billion in organic inflows, and announced a $35 billion private-credit financing partnership with Broadcom tied to its AI platform.

Management maintained its outlook for more than 20% FRE growth in 2026 and 10% annual SRE growth, supported by rising asset-management AUM, Athene's expanding invested assets and strong investment performance.

Baggage Claim: Apollo's $7.7 Billion Bid to Acquire easyJet

Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO) reported record second-quarter fee-related earnings and spread-related earnings, citing momentum in origination, capital formation and investment performance across its asset management and retirement services businesses.

The alternative asset manager generated fee-related earnings, or FRE, of $785 million, or $1.26 per share, up 25% from a year earlier and 8% sequentially. Spread-related earnings, or SRE, reached a record $877 million, or $1.41 per share. Together, the two core earnings streams produced adjusted net income of $1.3 billion, or $2.11 per share.

→ SpaceX's First Earnings Report Could Decide Whether Shorts or Bulls Have Control

As Broadcom Eclipses $2 Trillion, Private Credit Giants Wants In

CEO Marc Rowan said the quarter was "really all about momentum," pointing to growth in management fees, capital solutions fees, origination and inflows. Management fees rose 23% year over year to support FRE growth, while capital solutions fees reached $277 million, marking the fifth consecutive quarter above $200 million.

Origination and Capital Formation

Apollo originated $74 billion during the second quarter, bringing first-half origination to nearly $150 billion and trailing-12-month activity to nearly $320 billion. Rowan said the quarterly total did not include the company's announced $35 billion Broadcom financing because Apollo records originations when they close rather than when they are announced.

TPG Built a Record Year, Then Lost 40%—Is the Selloff Overdone?

The company said it had $50 billion of signed and announced transactions during the second quarter that are expected to benefit future periods. Rowan described the pipeline as the strongest Apollo has seen, tied to what the company calls a "global industrial renaissance."

Story Continues

President Jim Zelter said $68 billion of second-quarter originations were in debt, with approximately 75% investment grade and 25% sub-investment grade. Investment-grade originations generated spreads of 280 basis points over Treasuries, while sub-investment-grade originations generated spreads of 440 basis points over Treasuries, according to Zelter.

→ Why Rare Earth Processing Could Be the Real 2027 Opportunity

Apollo announced its $35 billion financing partnership with Broadcom during the quarter, which Zelter described as the largest private credit financing ever. The financing is intended to support Broadcom's AI XPV platform. CFO Martin Kelly said associated fees will be recognized as the financing is drawn down over multiple quarters, weighted toward the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first three quarters of 2027.

Total organic inflows reached a quarterly record of $60 billion, including $38 billion in asset management and $22 billion at Athene. The company said Athene had generated $42 billion of inflows during the first half and remained on pace to meet its $85 billion full-year target.

Asset Management Earnings and Fundraising

Kelly said asset management AUM rose 25% year over year, while fee-generating AUM increased 34%. Perpetual capital represented 60% of total AUM and 70% of fee-generating AUM. Apollo held $82 billion of dry powder at quarter-end, including $62 billion of future management-fee potential. Once deployed, that capital could generate approximately $400 million in annual management fee income, Kelly said.

The firm's FRE margin was 58.5%, up about 80 basis points sequentially and 120 basis points from the prior year. Kelly said Apollo remains on track for roughly 100 basis points of full-year margin expansion and reiterated its outlook for more than 20% FRE growth in 2026.

In fundraising, Apollo said its institutional business had broad-based demand across hybrid, multi-credit, asset-backed finance, direct lending, performing credit and private equity strategies. Its third direct-lending vintage was pulled forward and is expected to exceed its $5 billion predecessor, according to Zelter.

Apollo's flagship private equity Fund XI had surpassed $12 billion in commitments through July. Kelly said management fees for the fund are expected to begin in the latter part of the first half of 2027, depending on when the predecessor Montana fund is fully invested.

Retirement Services and Investment Performance

Athene's gross invested assets grew 14% year over year to $414 billion. Reported net spread was 114 basis points, compared with 97 basis points in the prior quarter. Kelly said the net spread would have been 10 basis points higher when adjusted to Apollo's 11% long-term return assumption for its alternatives portfolio, placing it within the company's prior 120- to 125-basis-point full-year outlook.

Apollo maintained its target for 10% SRE growth for the year, assuming an 11% return on the alternatives portfolio. The company also reported an approximately $700 million realized gain from Intel within Athene's GAAP results.

Zelter highlighted investment performance across the platform, including a 21% net internal rate of return for Fund X, compared with a 14% industry index return for the 2023 vintage. Apollo's AAA strategy recorded positive performance in 45 of the past 46 quarters, he said, while major credit strategies returned between 7% and 11% over the past 12 months.

Market Infrastructure and Strategic Investments

Rowan emphasized Apollo's effort to make private-market assets more accessible to broader pools of investors by introducing daily pricing, identifiers, settlement capabilities and market-making infrastructure. The company went live with estimated daily net asset values for its investment-grade fixed-income suite on July 1 and expects daily pricing for all credit assets by Oct. 1.

Apollo's partnership with ICE is now live, with more than 2,000 ICE IDs assigned. Rowan said the company expects its debt and equity products to receive ICE IDs over time. Apollo also said more than $30 billion of its assets have traded through its market-making efforts, with volume continuing to double.

The company confirmed plans to open an office in Austin, Texas, which Rowan said will focus on building future businesses and processes while expanding access to a different workforce and a significant fundraising ecosystem.

On capital allocation, Apollo repurchased about $100 million of shares during the quarter. Over the past 12 months, it returned $1.6 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks, while investing nearly $500 million in strategic growth initiatives, including an investment in Athora.

Apollo Global Management, Inc (NYSE: APO) is a global alternative investment manager that specializes in private equity, credit and real assets. The firm originates, invests in and manages a broad set of strategies across distressed and opportunistic credit, direct lending, structured credit, buyouts and real estate. Apollo provides investment management and advisory services to institutional clients and individual investors through pooled funds, separate accounts and publicly listed investment vehicles.

news.Title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Intel: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
The semiconductor landscape is shifting rapidly as artificial intelligence demands redefine hardware requirements for global enterprises. Choosing between Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC) requires understanding their different approaches to this massive technological transition.

Advanced Micro Devices has transformed from a secondary player into a leader in high-performance computing and AI accelerators. Intel, traditionally the dominant force in PC and server processors, is currently reorganizing its business to include foundry services and specialized AI chips. This comparison examines their financials, market strategies, and risks to help you determine which investment path is better.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

Advanced Micro Devices designs high-performance and adaptive computing products, ranging from standard CPUs to advanced AI accelerators, within the semiconductor stocks category. It maintains essential relationships with cloud giants and console manufacturers like Sony Group Corp (NYSE:SONY) and Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT). Recently, the company partnered with OpenAI and Anthropic to deploy its latest GPU generations and acquired ZT Systems' design business to scale its infrastructure capabilities.

In FY 2025, revenue reached more than $34.6 billion, representing a significant 34% increase compared to the $25.8 billion recorded in the previous year. The company reported a net income of approximately $4.4 billion, which is a substantial rise from the $1.6 billion reported in 2024. Its net margin, which is the percentage of revenue left as profit, improved to roughly 12.5% during this period.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was a very low 0.1x, suggesting a conservative use of borrowed money. Free cash flow in 2025 was $5.5 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 21% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Intel Corp

Intel operates as an integrated device manufacturer, focusing on x86-based microprocessors and integrated graphics for PCs and data centers. The company also provides foundry services for semiconductor design, manufacturing, and assembly for external customers. It is currently navigating the complexities of its government-funded business model while managing high-profile shareholder lawsuits related to those deals.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $52.9 billion, a slight decrease of nearly 0.5% compared to the prior year. The company reported a net loss of close to $267 million for that fiscal period, though this was a marked improvement over the much larger loss in 2024. Its net margin was roughly negative 0.5%, reflecting the heavy research and manufacturing costs required to transform its business model.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.4x. The current ratio stood at close to 2.0x, and the company reported negative free cash flow of more than $4.9 billion for FY 2025. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 25% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Advanced Micro Devices faces significant risks from U.S. government export controls on advanced AI semiconductors to China. These regulations threaten its revenue from high-end products like the MI308 GPU. It also faces intense competition from Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Intel while relying heavily on third-party foundries such as TSMC and GlobalFoundries Inc (NASDAQ:GFS) for its manufacturing needs.

Intel faces pressure from competitors like Advanced Micro Devices and Nvidia, who have captured significant market share in the high-growth AI and server sectors. The company is also subject to shareholder lawsuits stemming from its government deals, which creates financial and reputational exposure. Furthermore, the company remains vulnerable to cyclical industry downturns as it attempts to shift its focus from PCs to AI silicon.

Valuation comparison

Intel carries a higher Forward P/E , measuring price against future earnings estimates, while Advanced Micro Devices has a higher P/S ratio, which compares price to revenue.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Intel is pressing on with its plan to revive its business. This spring it announced a partnership with Space Exploration Technologies Inc (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) to build Terafab, a massive AI chip-making plant aiming to produce as many as 200 billion AI chips a year. Intel is providing its foundry expertise and its 14A process, an effort to produce 1.4-nanometer chips it announced two years ago and is still developing. Also this year, Intel signed a deal with Nvidia to help build a new AI GPU called Crescent Island that can work in tandem with Nvidia's Blackwell AI chips, and agreed to help develop an AI-centric chip for the Google division of Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG), too. Last year, the company raised investments from the U.S. government and SoftBank to improve its capital position.

All that has generated some optimism on Wall Street. For fiscal 2026, sales are seen rising 19% to $62.3 billion, though a large $11 billion net loss is projected, part of the cost of expanding its foundries in the U.S.

AMD, meanwhile, is riding the wave of a late 2025 deal to supply OpenAI with chips, potentially worth billions of dollars. Management believes the shift from large language models and generative AI to agentic AI and robotic AI will create even more demand for AMD's style of chips. The company now expects demand for AI-related chips to rise more than 30% annually, up sharply from an estimate executives had provided at the start of 2026.  On top of the AI strength, the business has notched impressive wins in healthcare and financial services in recent months.

All of that has analysts expecting AMD to ring up sales of $49.6 billion, a jump of more than 40% year over year, with net income of $8.7 billion.

news.Title: Dear Cisco Stock Fans, Earnings Are Just Around the Corner
news.Content:
A particular kind of pressure comes from performing well. Cisco Systems (CSCO) built it for itself. After a fiscal third quarter that blew past its own guidance, the company is now walking into its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 report, due in the coming weeks, with expectations it essentially wrote.

Artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending is pouring into Cisco's order book, enterprises are in the thick of a campus networking refresh cycle, and routing demand hasn't cooled off. Then there's Cisco's growing push into AI-powered security and observability. It's a signal that the company is expanding its stake in the infrastructure that makes AI work. Further, both revenue and EPS posted double-digit growth, and the company beat estimates on both lines.

Now, with Q4 guidance pointing to another quarter of double-digit growth, investors will be watching closely to see whether Cisco can maintain that streak and justify the growing optimism surrounding its AI-led transformation.

About Cisco Stock

Headquartered in San Jose, California, Cisco develops networking, cybersecurity, collaboration, cloud, data center, wireless, Webex, analytics, and managed service technologies. With a market cap of $456.7 billion, it provides networking infrastructure, security, observability, communication, technical support, consulting, and managed services.

Cisco's shares have rewarded shareholders handsomely during the past year. Shares have climbed 76.9% over the last 52 weeks, including an impressive 49.3% gain in just the past six months.

From a valuation standpoint, CSCO stock is trading at 27.09 times forward adjusted price-to-earnings and 7.26 times forward sales. Both multiples sit above the industry averages as well as the company's own five-year averages, suggesting investors continue to assign the stock a premium valuation.

Meanwhile, dividend investors have quieter reasons to like the stock. The company has increased its dividend for 14 consecutive years and currently pays an annual dividend of $1.68 per share, translating to a 1.45% yield. Its latest quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share was distributed on July 22 to shareholders of record as of July 6.

Cisco Surpasses Q3 Earnings

Story Continues

Cisco reported its fiscal third-quarter 2026 results on May 13, triggering a positive market reaction. The stock gained 2.6% on the day of the announcement before rallying another 13.4% in the following trading session.

Revenue climbed 12% year-over-year (YOY) to $15.8 billion, comfortably ahead of analysts' expectations of $15.55 billion. Non-GAAP EPS increased 10.4% from the prior-year period to $1.06, beating the Street's estimate of $1.04.

Growth remained broad-based across the business. Product revenue rose 17%, supported once again by robust demand for AI infrastructure and campus networking solutions. Meanwhile, services revenue came in at $3.7 billion, down 1% YOY, primarily because of the timing of service contract renewals.

Strong customer demand was evident across Cisco's order book. Total product orders increased 35% YOY during the quarter. Excluding hyperscaler customers, whose orders expanded at a triple-digit rate, product orders still advanced 19%, highlighting healthy demand across enterprise markets.

Networking continued to lead the way. Networking product orders jumped more than 50%, campus networking orders grew more than 25%, and data center switching orders increased by over 40% YOY. These results underscore broad-based strength across Cisco's core networking portfolio.

Demand from hyperscale customers also continued to accelerate. AI infrastructure orders reached $5.3 billion year-to-date (YTD), prompting Cisco to raise its fiscal 2026 AI infrastructure order outlook to $9 billion. Also, the company lifted its projected AI infrastructure revenue target to $4 billion, up from $3 billion, reflecting confidence in sustained long-term demand and an expanding multi-year global campus networking refresh cycle.

Looking ahead, management expects Q4 revenue to range between $16.7 billion and $16.9 billion, with non-GAAP EPS projected between $1.16 and $1.18. For the full year FY2026, Cisco forecasts revenue of $62.8 billion to $63 billion, while non-GAAP EPS is expected to come in between $4.27 and $4.29.

On the other hand, analysts expect Q4 FY2026 EPS to increase 22.2% YOY to $0.99. Over the longer term, estimates call for full-year FY2026 EPS of $3.54, representing 15.3% YOY growth, followed by another 13.3% increase to $4.01 in fiscal 2027.

What Do Analysts Expect for Cisco Stock?

Wall Street maintains a cautiously optimistic stance on Cisco, assigning it an overall rating of "Moderate Buy." Among 25 analysts covering the stock, 14 rate it a "Strong Buy," one recommends "Moderate Buy," and 10 advise investors to "Hold" the stock.

The average price target of $130.27 implies potential upside of 7.2%. Meanwhile, the Street-High target of $150 points to a possible gain of 23.4% from current levels.

news.Title: Apple-OpenAI Fight Takes Unexpected Turn
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) has escalated its legal battle with OpenAI by seeking a preliminary injunction that would restrict the ChatGPT maker and two former Apple employees from using or sharing alleged trade secrets. The request raises the stakes in a dispute that could influence OpenAI's expansion into consumer hardware and intensify its emerging competition with Apple.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with SSNLF.

Is AAPL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

In a filing submitted Monday, Aug. 3, Apple asked a U.S. district court to temporarily block OpenAI and former employees Chang Liu and Tang Yew Tan from accessing, obtaining, using or disclosing the disputed information while the lawsuit proceeds.

Apple argued that it could be irreparably harmed without immediate court intervention. The company also requested expedited evidence gathering related to the alleged confidential material and permission to question Liu, Tan and OpenAI employee Yu-Ting Peng.

Apple is additionally seeking testimony from representatives of io Products, OpenAI's hardware operation, and an unnamed OpenAI employee who previously worked at Apple.

The legal fight stems from Apple's lawsuit filed last month, which accused OpenAI of obtaining confidential information to support its push into consumer devices. OpenAI rejected the allegations and opposed the injunction, saying it neither possesses nor wants Apple's trade secrets.

The dispute matters because OpenAI's planned hardware entry could expand its rivalry with Apple beyond software and AI assistants into devices that compete for consumer attention and potentially challenge the iPhone-centered ecosystem.

Apple shares were already under pressure, falling 1.78% Monday and more than 11% over five trading sessions following a weaker-than-expected revenue outlook.

Investor Takeaway On Apple Stock

Investors should watch whether the court grants Apple's injunction and how broadly any restrictions apply. A favorable ruling could delay OpenAI's hardware development or limit its access to former Apple talent and technical knowledge.

A denial would weaken Apple's immediate legal leverage and allow OpenAI's device strategy to proceed with fewer constraints. The larger risk is strategic rather than near-term financial: OpenAI could eventually create a new consumer computing platform that competes with Apple's hardware, services and control of the user interface.

news.Title: Intel vs. TSMC: Intel Is Winning an AI Battle Against TSMC That Few Investors Are Watching
news.Content: It is not often that TSMC (TSM) takes cues from Intel (INTC), but that is undoubtedly what's happening. news.AI_Summary:
• TSMC is reportedly developing a new packaging technology, referred to as 'EMIB-like,' modeled after Intel's EMIB technology.
• This development signifies a shift where TSMC is taking cues from Intel in the competitive AI chip packaging space.
• Intel's EMIB technology is considered cheaper and potentially better suited for large AI chip designs compared to TSMC's CoWoS.
• TSMC's CoWoS is sold out into 2027, pushing customers to seek alternatives, with Intel's EMIB-T achieving a 98% yield rate and attracting interest from major tech companies.
• While TSMC maintains a lead, Intel is gaining ground in packaging, a critical battleground for AI chips.

news.Title: 權值股休兵小兵齊衝鋒！華邦電領記憶體族群亮燈救火｜Yahoo財經掃描
news.Content:

news.Title: 謝再居臨危接棒延續三大業務　盼達成黃崇仁發股利遺願
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年08月4日電）晶圓代工廠力積電 (6770) 董事長黃崇仁於7月31日因心肺衰竭離世，由副董事長謝再居代理董事長職務。謝再居今天表示，會在現有基礎下，延續記憶體、邏輯代工及AI封裝所需各種半導體零件業務，盼達成黃崇仁交代未來都會有股利的心願，希望力積電股東能夠放心。

力積電今天舉行媒體交流會，謝再居與總經理朱憲國出面說明黃崇仁逝世後力積電的營運發展方向。

謝再居說，黃崇仁逝世的消息非常令人震驚，近日可說是「兵荒馬亂」，沒有預期這麼早要處理這事情。他2年前辭去總經理職務，轉任副董事長，原本打算退休，如今在員工的期待下出面主持大局，要承擔比以前更多的責任。

謝再居表示，經過幾天沉澱後，確認黃崇仁家屬會繼續支持營運團隊，在現有基礎下，延續記憶體、邏輯代工及AI封裝所需各種半導體零件業務。

謝再居說，他的個性與黃崇仁有點相輔相成，在面對新的機會時，黃崇仁生性樂觀，自己則主要考量風險因素，有時候要拉黃崇仁一把；未來由他決定事情，可以預見未來風格是保守，「不會那麼衝」。

他表示，當前態勢對半導體有利，力積電是做代工，產品平均售價提升會有遞延效應，預期未來半年業績可望月月高升，營收與獲利都可以有不錯表現。

謝再居說，依照公司規章，力積電有賺錢時，每半年要分紅給股東一次，下個月的董事會也許就會決定上半年的分紅。若市場能夠維持，力積電未來每年可望獲利，希望能達成黃崇仁交代未來都會有股利的心願，並希望力積電股東能夠放心。

朱憲國則提出3個不變，第1是力積電本業向上沒有改變，8月起營收將會明顯往上走；第2是團隊沒有改變，營運正常，沒有受黃崇仁逝世影響；第3是未來方向也不會改變，3D AI代工業績將占總營收20%。

力積電副總經理譚仲民說，力積電將在南京東路三段的辦公室設置追思會場，自8月5日至12日開放外界預約追思，為黃崇仁最後送別。

譚仲民表示，目前還在籌組治喪委員會，台積電 (2330) 創辦人張忠謀同意出任治喪委員會榮譽主委。

譚仲民說，力積電最大法人股東力晶創新投資控股8月3日決定，由原總經理謝明霖升任董事長，未來雙方的策略合作不會有大變化。（編輯：張良知）

半導體與權值股方面，盤中半導體與AI概念股一度帶動反彈，愛德萬測試(6857.JP)、軟銀集團(9984.JP)等權值股先獲買盤青睞，但在獲利了結浮現後轉為壓抑指數的主因。相較之下，Kioxia Holdings(285A.JP)、KOKUSAI ELECTRIC(6525.JP)、Lasertec(6920.JP)等個股維持相對強勢，顯示資金仍集中在題材明確的標的。

類股輪動方面，類股表現分歧，非鐵金屬、玻璃與土石製品、機械類股表現相對強勢；食品、保險、資訊與通信類股則承壓。盤面沒有形成全面性上攻，而是以個別類股與個股輪動為主，反映市場對財報與展望的觀望心態仍重。

news.Title: 《台股盤後》震盪小跌25點，月線得而復失
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-08-04 15:42:38 新聞中心 發佈

美股電子盤延續週一正常盤漲勢下，台股今(4)日早盤雖一度因聯發科/日月光投控見獲利了結賣壓、下跌近500點並失守43000點關卡，但在跌深股國巨*、週一弱勢股台達電及南亞帶動其它台塑三寶轉強，且記憶體股南亞科漲停、PCB族群的台光電及欣興強攻下，加權指數盤中一度翻紅，惟午盤後國泰金、台積電轉弱影響下，終場收在43360.66點、日K連三紅，小跌25.75點或0.06%、月線得而復失，成交量增至1兆362億元。

科技巨擘、AI概念股強彈，再加上美伊緊張局勢降溫、帶動油價與美國公債殖利率雙雙走軟，美國四大指數在8月第一個交易日全面跳高。亞洲股市方面，日經225指數今日以紅盤開出後，因韓股三星電子、SK HYNIX走弱致日本部分半導體相關股走跌，拖累日經指數翻黑，一度下挫近900點，隨後跌勢收斂，終場上漲0.32%；韓國股市震盪收紅，KOSPI終場上漲1.62%。

台股今日電子族群漲跌互見，台積電收在2320元，下跌2.11%，聯發科、鴻海都有超過1%的跌幅，日月光投控跌逾4%。不過市場看好記憶體需求持續升溫，記憶體族群獲資金點火，南亞科、華邦電亮燈漲停，旺宏、十銓、力成、旺宏等也都漲勢凌厲，另外ABF載板三雄今日也表現亮眼，南電、景碩都衝上漲停，欣興也漲逾6%。

從29大類股表現來看，今日以玻璃陶瓷類股最為強勢，漲幅達9.34%，其中台玻、中釉都漲停；光電類股在大立光漲停激勵下，上漲4.88%；電子零組件類股上漲4.46%，包含川湖、健策等都亮燈漲停。在跌勢部分，建材營造股下跌2.02%、跌幅最重，運動休閒、半導體、觀光餐旅、水泥類股也相對疲軟，跌幅都超過1%。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人總計買超1.09億元；其中，外資及陸資(不含外資自營商)賣超57.31億元，投信買超252.7億元，自營商賣超194.28億元。

news.Title: 世界先進：第3季出貨量看增3%　產能利用率估90%
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中台北2026年08月4日電）晶圓代工廠世界先進 (5347) 總經理尉濟時今天表示，客戶對於電源管理產品需求持續增長，不過，因設備產生的限制，預期第3季晶圓出貨量將季增1%至3%，產能利用率將提升至90%，產品平均售價揚升2%至4%。

世界先進今天召開線上法人說明會，說明第2季營運結果。世界先進第2季晶圓出貨量71.3萬片，季增11%，表現符合預期，產品平均售價上揚3%，單季營收新台幣142.45億元，季增13.7%。

受惠較佳的產能利用率與產品組合，以及價格上揚，第2季毛利率攀升至32.3%，較第1季揚升3個百分點，歸屬母公司淨利29.75億元，季增32.4%，每股純益1.56元。世界先進上半年營收267.76億元，歸屬母公司淨利52.21億元，每股純益2.84元。

展望未來，尉濟時說，客戶對於電源管理晶圓需求持續成長，不過，因設備產生的限制，第3季晶圓出貨量將季增約1%至3%，產品平均銷售單價上揚2%至4%，毛利率介於32.5%至34.5%。

尉濟時表示，客戶對AI伺服器電源管理產品以及季節性備貨需求持續增長，目前訂單能見度約4個月，第3季產能利用率將提升至90%，第4季可望高於90%水準。

尉濟時指出，新加坡12吋廠已於6月順利產出首批晶圓，良率超過99%，將如期於2027年第1季量產。為滿足客戶需求，將汰換、升級部分粗線寬產能至細線寬，2026年資本支出將與2025年相當，約新台幣600億至700億元。

世界先進董事長方略說，持續調漲價格已無可避免，目前已與客戶協調2027年價格調整，考量成本上漲趨勢與產能建置所需費用，2027年漲價幅度應不會比2026年小。

news.Title: 台股爆千點震盪！台積電收盤慘跌50元 上攻最大壓力曝光
news.Content:
台股短線反彈漲多後今（4日）出現震盪，盤中一度翻紅漲逾500點，但月季線套牢賣壓仍沉重，加上外資持續部署空單，已衝破9萬口再創新高，多空激戰使高低震盪逾千點，近午盤時翻黑，終場下跌25.75點，收在43360.66點。

權值股台積電劇烈波動，高低落差達55元，最終下跌50元收在2320元；聯發科下跌45元或1.15%，收在3865元；台達電上漲40元收在1620元；鴻海小跌3元收在250元。

大型權值股表現普通，跌深的中小型股較為強勢，記憶體、矽光子及被動元件等仍是主流，押寶法說行情，南亞科、華邦電及力積電強鎖漲停，鈺創與晶豪科也同步亮燈。

記憶體看誰表演？主流族群怎挑？

分析師周代運日前指出，記憶體族群是當前盤勢最紮實的主流類股，南亞科為絕對核心，DRAM正式從景氣循環轉為AI結構性長期缺貨，一路吃到2028年，低檔長抱毫無問題，拉回無量回檔才考慮加碼，絕對禁止追高搶進。

另外，許多投資人關注旺宏、華邦電、力積電、創見及群聯的狀況，周代運認為，套牢者應該利用本次反彈，減碼弱勢的力積電、旺宏騰出現金，集中加碼南亞科，才是最快解套方式。

台股後市壓力大 套牢賣壓還有多少？

展望台股後市，分析師李蜀芳認為，月均線呈現下彎扣高，這條均線將形成強大反壓，即便股價衝過也容易因慣性而拉回，因此應尊重月線反壓，不宜在月線之上盲目追高。

操作建議上，李蜀芳指出，日均線（周線）的正乖離已大於4%，短線震盪在所難免，強勢股若要續強則必須守住五日線，應利用15日財報公佈前的反彈期進行「汰弱留強」，並盡量使用現股操作，避開多殺多的風險。

news.Title: 台股指數小跌，CPO、ABF、記憶體、矽晶圓、設備族群輪流彈升
news.Content:
【財訊快報／方亞申】美伊戰爭談談打打，國際股市經過回檔後開始展開反彈，但亞洲股市表現持續力較差，金融市場焦點正轉向美日政府聯合出手干預日圓匯市，日圓止貶快速升值，亞洲貨幣才會止貶。週一美國道瓊及標普指數以收盤而言皆創歷史新高，那指跟著強彈，費半反彈走勢倒是較弱勢。亞洲股市週二普遍小漲、小跌居多。台股壓著台積電(2330)、聯發科(2454)、鴻海(2317)、日月光(3711)等權值股，指數空間就受限；但中小型電子股族群快速輪動，CPO、ABF、記憶體、矽晶圓、衛星族群各自表現；金融股則元大金走勢最強。指數終場下跌25.75點或0.06%，收在43360.66點，成交量10362.81億元。美股週一盤前傳出美伊將簽字和談，使得道瓊及標普指數持續大漲，盤中高點都已接近歷史新高，並創收盤歷史新高。許久未表現的那指，在谷歌、亞馬遜、輝達、臉書等股價強勁上揚下，也出現少見的長紅幾乎站上季線。只有費半雖也反彈但走勢較弱。但是伊朗方面否認和彈，各說各話已經一陣子了，所幸只要油價在80-85美元之下，金融市場壓力就較小。電子股中記憶體族群漲跌互見，不如之前強勢。倒是CPO相關的Lumemtum及Coherent股價大漲超過9%，算力出租相關的NBIS以及康寧股價也大漲，這都跟輝達有關，而輝達股價少見的上漲2.93%，顯示對於AI仍相當注意。而科技巨頭亞馬遜、微軟、谷歌甚至連臉書近期走勢也相當強，亞馬遜還創新高，總市值進入3兆元俱樂部，顯示市場資金還是多。只要四大指數在季線之上就屬強勢。

亞洲日圓在美日政府干預下快速從163.98升值至157.5附近，日股拉回；韓股看三星及海力士臉色，週二早盤還是屬於下跌。日、韓股市小漲、小跌整理，台股相對指數上檔空間不會太大，由於外資期貨空單超過9萬口歷史新高，指數上漲空間被壓抑，各族群輪流反彈，週一台股上市櫃指數收紅而融資就轉為小幅增加，籌碼面不是太好。台積電股價持續小拉回，前五大權值股中日月光、聯發科、鴻海皆回檔，台達電(2308)跌深反彈。較佳情況是緯創(3231)股價持續走高，緯穎(6669)股價創歷史新高。帶動代工股英業達(2356)、和碩(4938)、仁寶(2324)等上漲。機殼的勤誠(8210)、CCL的台光電(2383)、台燿(6274)、滑軌的川湖(2059)上漲，股價創新高。智邦(2345)反彈在前而拉回，AI零組件族群大家底部皆出現。

上市指數反彈較無力，但是中小型的櫃買指數卻強勁反彈，主要在政策放寬關緊閉條件，所以櫃買指數三連中長紅。其中CPO相關股聯亞(3081)、聯鈞(3450)、眾達(4977)、波若威(3163)、IET(4971)、華星光(4979)、光環(3234)、前鼎(4908)、統新(6426)、光聖(6442)全面大漲；記憶體則有華邦電(2344)、南亞科(2408)、十銓(4967)大漲；ABF則有欣興(3037)、景碩(3189)、南電(8046)；矽晶圓則有台勝科(3532)、環球晶圓(6488)漲停。被動元件禾伸堂(3026)、國巨*(2327)續彈但感覺幅度較有限。衛星方面昇達科(3491)、啟碁(6285)、華通(2313)、萊德(7717)表現佳。設備部分弘塑(3131)、萬潤(6187)、大量(3167)、盟立(2464)、由田(3455)等等表現都很好。

傳產股台塑四寶及華新(1605)走勢都不弱。金融股則有元大金(2885)還原除息前股價創歷史高。反彈行其中大家輪彈，但震盪幅度會很大，操作上宜謹慎。

news.Title: 權值股承壓，指數受制月線，各族群輪動櫃買連續大漲
news.Content:
【財訊快報／方亞申】美伊戰爭談談打打，國際股市經過回檔後開始展開反彈，只要油價未再站上100美元之上，金融市場焦點正轉向美日政府聯合出手干預日圓匯市，日圓止貶，亞洲貨幣才會止貶。週一美國道瓊及標普指數以收盤而言皆創歷史新高，那指跟著強彈，費半反彈走勢倒是較弱勢。亞洲股市週二開盤普遍小跌，盤中小漲小跌居多。台股壓著台積電(2330)，電子股快速輪動，CPO、ABF、記憶體、矽晶圓、衛星以及老AI族群各自表現；金融股則以元大金(2885)走勢最強。預估週二成交量超過1兆元。亞洲日圓在美日政府干預下快速從163.98升值至157.5附近，日股拉回，要等到匯市平穩股市才有機會有大表現。韓股看三星及海力士臉色，週二早盤還是屬於下跌。日韓股市小漲小跌整理，台股相對指數上漲空間不會太大，各族群輪流反彈。不過週一台股上市櫃指數收紅而融資就轉為小幅增加，籌碼面不是太好。由於外資期貨空單超過9萬口歷史新高，指數上漲空間被壓抑，台積電股價持續小拉回，前五大權值股中日月光(3711)、聯發科(2454)也回檔，台達電(2308)跌深反彈、鴻海(2317)亦同。較佳情況是緯創(3231)股價持續走高，緯穎(6669)股價創歷史新高。帶動代工股英業達(2356)、和碩(4938)、仁寶(2324)等上漲。而老AI零組件的散熱奇鋐(3017)、雙鴻(3324)以及CCL的台光電(2383)、台燿(6274)、滑軌的川湖(2059)也上漲，智邦(2345)反彈在前，大家底部皆出現。

上市指數反彈較無力但是中小型的櫃買指數卻強勁反彈，主要在政策放寬關緊閉條件，所以櫃買指數三連中長紅。

CPO相關股聯亞(3081)、聯鈞(3450)、眾達(4977)、波若威(3163)、IET(4971)、華星光(4979)、光環(3234)、前鼎(4908)、統新(6426)、光聖(6442)全面大漲；記憶體則有華邦電(2344)、南亞科(2408)、十銓(4967)大漲；ABF則有欣興(3037)、景碩(3189)、南電(8046)；矽晶圓則有台勝科(3532)、環球晶圓(6488)漲停。被動元件禾伸堂(3026)漲停，國巨*(2327)續彈。衛星方面昇達科(3491)、啟碁(6285)表現佳。設備部分弘塑(3131)、萬潤(6187)、大量(3167)等等表現都很好。

傳產股台塑四寶及華新(1605)走勢都不弱。金融股則有元大金還原除息前股價創歷史高。台股正處反彈，大家輪彈，但震盪幅度會很大，操作上宜謹慎。

news.Title: Why Arm Holdings Stock Lost 34% in July
news.Content: Shares of Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM) were pulling back last month on broader concerns about the AI boom, and as the stock may have gotten overheated in the second quarter. Chip stocks fell broadly last month as investors questioned the durability of the AI boom, including whether hyperscalers would ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Arm Holdings (ARM) stock declined 34% in July due to broader concerns about the AI boom's durability and potential overheating.
• Investors questioned hyperscalers' ROI on AI infrastructure investments, leading to a broad sell-off in chip stocks.
• Despite a valuation concern from HSBC (rating lowered to Hold), Arm's Q1 earnings report exceeded estimates, with data center royalty revenue doubling YoY.
• The company forecasts $15 billion in CPU revenue and $25 billion in overall revenue by fiscal 2031, with a key test being the rollout of its new AGI CPU in fiscal Q4.
news.Keywords: AI boom concerns, valuation, data center revenue, earnings report, stock decline

news.Title: 存儲三巨頭明年產能傳售罄，AI需求推升供應短缺與價格高檔常態化
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】外電報導，市場傳出，三星電子(韓股代碼005930)、美光(Micron，美股代碼MU)及SK海力士(韓股代碼000660，美股代碼SKHY)的DRAM與高頻寬記憶體(HBM)2027年產能已全數分配完畢；三星、美光及SanDisk(美股代碼SNDK)的NAND Flash產能也大致預售一空。鎧俠(285A.T)與SK海力士預計最遲於8月底完成分配，印證業界對2027年可能成為存儲史上最短缺一年的預警。AI伺服器需求成為本輪供給緊張的核心動力，主要原廠陸續與雲端服務商及AI大廠簽訂3-5年期長期供貨協議，部分交易更採用預付訂金模式。業界估計，HBM及AI伺服器相關應用可能占用約七成DRAM產能，原廠亦優先把先進製程及封裝資源分配給毛利較高的AI產品。

在總產能擴張速度有限的情況下，手機及個人電腦業者可取得的DRAM配額可能明顯減少，實際供應量甚至僅達原定需求的六至七成。尚未提前鎖定2027年產能的買家，除可能被迫接受更高價格，也面臨即使願意加價仍難以取得足夠供貨的風險，顯示存儲市場正從傳統現貨循環轉向長約主導的賣方格局。

NAND供應商數量雖多於DRAM，市場也擔心新產能釋出及消費電子需求疲弱，可能令2027年下半年供需逐步轉向寬鬆，但企業級固態硬碟(SSD)及近線硬碟需求仍受到AI數據中心擴建支撐。業界預期，2027年DRAM與NAND價格漲幅可能較2026年的倍數式上漲收斂，但供應持續偏緊、價格維持高檔及長期協議提前鎖量，將成為存儲產業的新常態。

news.Title: 台股第2隻腳成形！法人喊買20檔 台積電、鴻海、聯亞、華碩、國泰金…目標價EPS一表看
news.Content:
台股7月回檔逾3006點，月跌6.5%，創史上月跌點第2大，主因受到韓股熔斷、美伊衝突再起與Fed升息預期等，大盤加速趕底，第2隻腳成形，法人看好AI基本面依然穩固，實體AI應用商機擴大，8月推5大選股策略，包括AI算力、先進封裝、光通訊、實體AI商機和旺季暨殖利率股等，點名台積電、中砂、全新、研華、寶雅等20檔買進，目標價EPS一口氣全說了。

金控龍頭旗下投顧表示，當前總經影響資本市場有2大因素：第一、韓股熔斷所引起的籌碼面踩踏；其次是高利率對股票投資的抑制效應。韓股一再發生熔斷，7/29 KOPSI回測5200點，距6/22高點9385點下跌逾4成，年至今漲幅降至3成以內，指數快速修正後籌碼壓力已大為釋放。

再者、高利率對長期股票投資的抑制壓力，7月美伊衝突再起，油價自6月修正低點69美元反彈至80美元以上；7/29聯準會(Fed)FOMC如市場預期維持3.5%-3.75%利率不變，華許重申2%的通膨目標，油價反彈使市場升息預期回升，美30年公債殖利率突破5.2%，不僅挫傷美國房市復甦及通膨率回降至2%機會，當股利率低於長債利率，亦將使長期投資股票的買盤積極性降低，不利股市投資信心與指數向上空間。

近期AI類股的股價出現大幅修正，市場雜訊湧現，包括：(1)擔心CSP(雲端服務供應商)業者擴大支出後的低資本回報率及自由現金流量轉負；(2)中國半導體自主提高與低成本AI模型所帶來的威脅；3)新AI平台及技術，如Kyper機櫃(GPU改垂直排列)、高壓直流電(HVDC)、共同封裝光學(CPO)等遞延上市。

但投顧認為，近期投資人大幅拋售半導體、記憶體和其他晶片類股票，主要仍受韓股去槓桿所拖累，由第2季財報及第3季展望來看，目前AI基本面依然穩固。就下游ODM(代工)廠商來看，Kyber機櫃的延誤並不會造成太大影響，包括零組件相關供應廠商，因為原本預期短期貢獻度都不高。

另一方面，投顧對CPU(中央處理器)供應鏈、SPE(半導體生產設備)供應鏈以及TPU(Google客製化AI晶片)未來幾年強勁動能仍具信心。整體而言，還是看好技術領先還有規格升級趨勢下受惠的公司，不管是上游的半導體，或是下游的零組件。

康寧提出新CPO架構後，反可望提升市場規模成長

提升AI投資變現速度將是未來CSP業者的策略焦點，有鑑於此，預期8月舉行的台灣機器人與智慧自動化展、以及北京世界機器人大會將會展出更多樣的實體AI應用，尤其針對AI機器人開發的新一代晶片，更能主動式解決問題甚至優化作業效果，預料將促使企業、製造業加大後續採購力道，有利於國內關鍵零組件供應鏈。

此外，Space X首次成功試射第3代衛星V3，Amazon也提出擴大具D2D(手機直連衛星功能)的衛星發射計畫，接下來地面接收系統以及資訊控制中心的相關投資將明顯增溫，對已積極推出相關方案的網通業者、IPC(工業電腦)業者帶來成長動能，亦有助於零組件業者如PCB(印刷電路板)/CCL(銅箔基板)、被動元件、記憶體等帶來新的規格升級動能。 投顧8月選股有5大策略說明如下：

策略1：AI算力

CSP業者甚至大型企業對於AI算力基礎設施的投資並未減緩，下半年聚焦輝達Vera Rubin實際出貨帶來之營運動能，以及企業級邊緣AI裝置出貨量大增等議題，看好台積電(2330)目標價3500元、緯穎(6669)6340元、鴻海(2317)323元。

策略2：先進封裝資本支出

台積電最新法說除釋出優異的財報與財測展望外，更重要的是提升今明兩年的資本支出規劃，尤其著重加大先進封裝領域的投資力道，並且將持續提升在地化供應鏈比重，看好中砂(1560)目標價800元、家登(3680)730元、志聖(2467)480元、兆聯(6944)1212元等。

news.Title: CSP明年ASIC端半導體產能瓶頸打開，博通、世芯、創意、智原、聯發科旺
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】市調單位TrendForce提到，CSP提高資本支出年增90%，致使2026年AI server出貨年增上看31%，至於2027年，預估九大CSP總資本支出規模將擴大至1.3兆美元左右，年增率雖然收斂至近50%，但值得注意的是，CSP加大在ASIC端的投資和採購，晶片產能供應增加，明年會達到一個真正的新高峰，ASIC設計服務的主要廠商，包括博通、世芯-KY(3661)、創意(3443)、智原(3035)、聯發科(2454)。根據TrendForce最新AI server產業研究，因應AI基礎建設需求高漲，估計2026年全球九大雲端服務供應商(CSP)總資本支出將年增約90%。近期超大型CSP、Tier-2資料中心業者對NVIDIA GB/VR等整櫃式AI server方案的採購意願明顯提高，且Google、AWS新一代ASIC平台於2026下半年陸續放量，加上中系業者擴大採用本地AI方案以滿足雲端大型語言模型(LLM) AI需求，促使TrendForce上調2026年AI server出貨年成長幅度，從原先的28%更新為近31%。

TrendForce統計，2026年Google、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft、Oracle以及ByteDance、Tencent、Alibaba、Baidu等九大CSP資本支出將突破8,867億美元。北美五大業者除了合計占比近90%，各自的資本支出也多翻倍提升，反映出大型CSP廠持續擴建AI資料中心、GPU叢集、液冷散熱等新一代基礎設施，以應對生成式AI及大型模型快速成長帶來的算力需求。

觀察美系業者在AI晶片端的著力重點，TrendForce預期Google 2026至2027年都將側重自家TPU晶片發展，2027年出貨量有望繼續高速成長。AWS 2026年以NVIDIA GB300作為GPU AI server主力，自研ASIC也穩定出貨，預期至2027年量能將再擴大。Meta 2026年主要採用NVIDIA GB/VR、AMD Helios整櫃式方案，自研ASIC布局預計至2027年將明顯加速，為該公司長期降低AI基礎設施成本、提升推論效率的重要策略。

在中系CSP部分，隨著中國AI生態系進入新一輪建設週期，主要業者皆加速AI相關投資。預估2026年ByteDance、Tencent、Alibaba、Baidu的合計資本支出將年增逾80%，以ByteDance投入力道最大，主要用於較大規模AI資料中心、自研ASIC平台和GPU叢集等建置。

展望2027年，預估九大CSP總資本支出規模將擴大至1.3兆美元左右，年增率收斂至近50%，主要是反映高基期因素，並非AI投資趨緩。在AI Inference、Agentic AI、自研ASIC和新一代AI模型持續推升算力需求的情況下，預期整體CSP投資金額將續創新高紀錄，產業成長有望從原先以GPU擴張為主，轉為包含AI server、液冷散熱、先進封裝、高速互聯、電源和記憶體等基礎設施全面升級的態勢。

九大CSP總資本支出規模將擴大至1.3兆美元左右，年增率雖然收斂至近50%，但值得注意的是，非中資的CSP加大在ASIC端的投資和採購，受惠台灣半導體廠，包括晶圓代工的台積電，以及設計服務業者世芯-KY、創意、智原、聯發科，還有後段的日月光、矽品、京元電(2449)、欣銓(3264)、力成(6239)等，以及載板廠的欣興(3037)、景碩(3189)與南電(8046)。

值得注意的是，CSP業者正加大在ASIC的投資與採購，讓ASIC設計服務業者包括博通、創意、世芯-KY、智原與聯發科受益，但受限於先進製程與先進封裝產能供應不足，因此今年ASIC晶片整體產出的成長動能有壓，不過進入2027年後，半導體先進製程與先進封裝產能會進一步增量，上述五大晶片設計業者將明顯大受益。

news.Title: 《日股早盤》部分半導體軟、日經跌421點 鎧俠漲
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-08-04 10:40:06 蔡承啟 發佈

日經225指數4日以紅盤開出後，因韓股走軟，日本部分半導體相關股走跌，拖累日經指數翻黑，一度下挫近900點，早盤收盤(台北時間上午10點30分)跌0.66%或跌421.55點，暫收63,333.35點。

東證股價指數(TOPIX)早盤收盤跌0.59%或跌23.55點，暫收3,936.48點。

截至早盤收盤為止，東證Prime上漲家數587家、下跌家數919家、維持平盤家數45家。東證Prime成交額為5兆16億日圓。

就類股表現來看，截至早盤收盤為止，全部33類股中、有9類股上漲，其中以非鐵金屬類股漲幅最大，其次依序為玻璃土石製品、金屬製品和機械業。

根據MoneyDJ XQ全球贏家系統的報價顯示，截至日本股市4日早盤收盤(台北時間上午10點30分)為止，日圓相對於美元匯率貶值0.32%至157.67日圓兌1美元；日圓相對於美元匯率3日升值0.54%，連續第4個交易日走升，盤中最高升至155.21，創約3個月來(5月6日以來)新高水準。

就個股表現來看，科技廠軟銀集團(Softbank Group)早盤大跌3.71%、測試設備商愛德萬測試(Advantest)早盤大跌3.37%、晶圓切割機廠DISCO早盤跌0.71%。

日本媒體Kabutan指出，愛德萬、軟銀集團早盤跌幅分別為日經225指數帶來255.84點、160.91點跌點，跌點「貢獻度」分居日經指數成分股前2大。

NAND Flash廠鎧俠(Kioxia)早盤勁揚2.83%、生產AI資料中心用光纖的Fujikura早盤飆漲6.15%、古河電工早盤狂飆10.66%。

機器人廠FUJI早盤狂飆10.03%。 AI需求加持、訂單破紀錄，FUJI上修財測，營收、獲利將創下歷史新高紀錄。

news.Title: 軟銀重金押注OpenAI 台積電與記憶體供應鏈恐陷AI泡沫風險
news.Content:
商傳媒 ｜吳承岳／台北報導

日本軟銀集團近年來持續加碼投資人工智慧領導者OpenAI，截至2026年5月，累計投入及承諾金額已達646億美元。這項巨額投入約佔軟銀集團淨資產價值（NAV，公司在扣除負債後剩餘的資產價值）的三分之一，凸顯其對AI產業的高度信心。

然而，這份押注也讓市場分析人士對潛在風險表達擔憂。有觀點指出，一旦OpenAI的信用狀況出現問題，或整個AI產業發展不如預期，軟銀集團的財務表現將受到直接衝擊，進而可能透過日股領頭羊軟銀集團的股價，對日經指數造成壓力。特別是，日本股市的指數結構中，愛德萬測試（Advantest）和東京電子（Tokyo Electron）等半導體相關企業佔比約達兩成，這意味著「軟銀集團股價下跌」與「半導體相關股價下跌」可能形成雙重路徑，將AI產業的潛在衝擊波及日本市場。

對台灣而言，與AI產業的連結主要透過晶圓代工龍頭台積電（TSMC）及其相關半導體供應鏈。若美國AI需求不如預期，或者OpenAI及其他美國雲端企業的投資計畫有所調整，將直接影響輝達（NVIDIA）和超微半導體（AMD）等客戶的客製化AI晶片訂單，進而挑戰台積電先進製程與先進封裝的訂單預期。儘管台積電的技術優勢並未動搖，但目前股價與資本支出計畫所反映的「強勁需求」能否維持，成為市場關注焦點。

此外，AI對高頻寬記憶體（HBM）的龐大需求，使得南韓記憶體大廠三星電子（Samsung Electronics）與SK海力士（SK hynix）專注於HBM生產，這也間接導致傳統記憶體與特殊型記憶體供應吃緊，讓台灣記憶體業者如南亞科技、華邦電子、旺宏電子等，有機會受惠於價格上漲。然而，記憶體產業歷來波動劇烈，若HBM需求降溫，或這些大廠將產能轉回通用DRAM或NAND，台灣廠商現有的價格優勢可能迅速消失。有分析認為，AI熱潮不僅沒有消除記憶體產業的循環性質，反而可能加大其價格波動的幅度。

總體而言，AI泡沫的潛在風險已不僅限於美國股市。它已滲透到日本的日經指數結構、軟銀集團的資產負債表，以及熊本、北海道等地方經濟；也牽動著台灣台積電的資本支出與半導體國家戰略；更影響著韓國三星電子與SK海力士的獲利、出口與韓圜匯率。當美國AI需求預期下滑時，東亞地區將以不同的形式承受衝擊，例如日本反映在設備訂單與日經指數，台灣反映在台積電投資計畫與晶圓代工稼動率，韓國則反映在記憶體價格與出口數據。

news.Title: 華邦電3顆紅燈照亮記憶體！力積電跟進鎖漲停 分析師曝多頭關鍵
news.Content:
記憶體族群漲勢持續延燒，今（4）日邁入第三個交易日強攻，指標股華邦電（2344）開盤不久即亮出第三根漲停板，股價攻上157元，力積電（6770）也同步亮燈鎖漲停，帶動整體記憶體族群全面上攻。分析師指出，目前基本面並未出現明顯變化，這波反彈主要是技術面修正空方趨勢，若龍頭股能持續維持強勢，將有機會帶動族群由空翻多。

截止上午10時10分，華邦電亮燈鎖死在157元，成交量10.8萬張，另有逾4.2萬張委買單高掛。力積電、鈺創（5351）、晶豪科（3006）也跟進接連亮燈漲停。另外，南亞科（2408）也有逾9%漲幅。

華邦電將於本周四（6日）召開法說會，將釋出下半年營運展望，近期吸引不少買盤積極卡位。其自7月30日低點117元展開反攻，短短三個交易日連拉三根漲停板，股價一路攀升至157元，累計大漲逾3成。

顧德投顧分析師張家豪表示，記憶體族群在基本面與題材面未有任何改變，先前股價下跌主因在於趨勢翻空，而翻空的技術條件為 MACD 小於 0 且跌破五日均線。目前若要止跌，必須先破壞這種空方架構，例如近期部分個股開始站回五日均線，這代表空方暫時進入休息狀態，主力正試圖將空方架構打掉並進行拉抬。

張家豪分析，以指標股華邦電為例，若能連續展現強勢、第三天站上漲停，並持續站穩五日均線，將有助於帶動整體族群的信心，甚至讓族群趨勢有機會從空方轉向翻多。

張家豪強調，由於 7 月經歷一整個月的下跌，市場信心相當脆弱。因此明日將是關鍵，若華邦電不能守住漲停價位，或出現帶長上影線的走勢，好不容易回溫的散戶信心可能會再度受挫。

王詩婷／財經特派記者，主跑勞動部、半導體、生技等

news.Title: Arm Quietly Builds Its Next Big AI Advantage
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Arm Holdings ( NASDAQ:ARM ) has joined a $312 million funding round for artificial-intelligence chip startup Olix, helping lift the private company's valuation to $3.3 billion. The investment gives Arm strategic exposure to a potential challenger in AI inference, but investors should view it primarily as an ecosystem bet rather than an immediate earnings catalyst.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with MU.

Is ARM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

London-based Olix develops specialized processors designed to run trained AI models more efficiently. Its technology uses photonic interconnects, which move data between chips using light, and aims to reduce reliance on costly high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging and leading-edge manufacturing capacity. The company plans to sell complete server racks combining chips, networking equipment and software.

The round was led by Fundomo and included Arm, Hudson River Trading and Netflix ( NASDAQ:NFLX ) co-founder Reed Hastings. Olix's post-money valuation has more than tripled from just over $1 billion in February, when it raised $220 million. The rapid increase reflects intense investor demand for alternatives to Nvidia's ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) general-purpose GPUs as AI inference becomes a larger portion of data-center computing.

However, Olix remains pre-commercial. The company expects to complete its chip tape-out by the end of 2026 and deliver its first products in 2027. That leaves substantial manufacturing, software and customer-validation risk before the valuation can be supported by meaningful revenue. Former Wise finance chief Matt Briers has joined as chief financial officer as Olix prepares for that transition.

Investor Takeaway On Arm Stock

For Arm shareholders, the round reinforces management's push beyond smartphones and deeper into AI infrastructure. Arm recently reported record fiscal first-quarter revenue of $1.29 billion, up 22%, while data-center royalty revenue more than doubled.

Investors should watch whether Olix completes tape-out on schedule, names customers and proves its processors can deliver lower inference costs at scale. Arm's November 4 earnings report is the next major catalyst, with management guiding fiscal second-quarter revenue to approximately $1.38 billion, plus or minus $50 million. Olix would become strategically meaningful only if its eventual chips drive licensing or royalty revenue for Arm; the funding alone is unlikely to materially alter near-term results.

news.Title: Citi Spots Surprising Winners in Chip Demand Surge
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Advanced Micro Devices ( NASDAQ:AMD ) and Texas Instruments ( NASDAQ:TXN ) received renewed Buy endorsements from Citi on Monday, with the bank arguing that two powerful semiconductor trends remain intact: accelerating artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending and a broad recovery in analog-chip demand. The calls place AMD's approaching earnings report and TI's manufacturing strategy at the center of the sector's next test.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD sells high-performance CPUs and GPUs used in data centers, personal computers and gaming systems. Texas Instruments designs and manufactures analog and embedded chips that regulate power and process real-world signals across industrial equipment, vehicles and electronics.

Citi expects industrial analog-chip sales to grow 30% to 35% year over year, with automotive increasing 12% to 15% and personal electronics rising 6% to 8%. Higher prices and lead times stretching to 16 weeks suggest demand is tightening against available supply rather than merely benefiting from easy comparisons.

We expect ADI, ON, and MCHP to report similar end-market strength and pricing/lead-time dynamics, the analysts wrote. We remain buyers of TXN, our top analog pick, as its manufacturing capacity should position it to capture a greater share.

TI's latest results support that view. Second-quarter revenue jumped 23% to $5.46 billion, while operating profit increased 48%. Management guided third-quarter revenue to between $5.65 billion and $6.15 billion, indicating the recovery has further room to run.

For AMD, Citi pointed to rising capital expenditures from Alphabet and Amazon as evidence that hyperscaler AI demand remains strong.

We view hyperscalers' ongoing investment in AI infrastructure as supportive of our positive outlook on compute semis and are buyers of top pick AMD on GPU/CPU share gains, Citi analysts wrote in a note to clients.

Investor Takeaway On AMD Stock

AMD reports second-quarter results Tuesday, August 4, after the market closes, making data-center revenue, Instinct GPU deployments and server-CPU momentum the immediate catalysts. AMD previously guided for approximately $11.2 billion in revenue and a 56% adjusted gross margin.

For TI, investors should monitor whether stronger utilization and pricing translate into sustained margin expansion and free cash flow. Weakening orders or shorter lead times would challenge Citi's recovery thesis, while continued industrial growth would strengthen TI's case for capturing share through its expanded manufacturing capacity.

The company is expected to have benefited from accelerating semiconductor demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments across DRAM, NAND and advanced logic/foundry markets. Semiconductor revenues are expected to increase in the high teens sequentially and more than 25% year over year. Strong demand for remote plasma and microwave products used in advanced DRAM, dissolved gas solutions for leading-edge logic nodes and lasers for back-end semiconductor applications is likely to have supported the to-be-reported quarter. Increasing NAND equipment upgrades, growing investments in advanced packaging and rising deposition and etch intensity are expected to have driven demand for the company's vacuum, power and plasma solutions.

In the Electronics and Packaging segment, MKSI is set to benefit from continued strength in chemistry and chemistry equipment, as well as laser drilling systems. AI is driving increased complexity and layer counts in advanced circuit board manufacturing, leading to higher demand for deposition, etch and chemistry equipment. Second quarter 2026 revenues in this segment are expected to grow in the high single digits sequentially and more than 30% year over year, with particular strength in flexible PCB drilling for high-end smartphones, wearables and rigid PCB applications related to the low earth orbit satellite market.

However, gross margin was 47% in the first quarter of 2026, but management noted a year-over-year decline tied to incremental tariff impacts. The company's second-quarter 2026 outlook assumes the current tariff environment. In the first quarter of 2026, tariff costs were largely neutralized dollar for dollar, yet the company expects a 30 bps to 40 bps gross margin impact that is included in the second-quarter guide. For the second quarter of 2026, MKSI anticipates a gross margin of 47% (+/- 1%).

Specialty Industrial revenues were $291 million in the first quarter of 2026, down 2% sequentially due to Lunar New Year seasonality. While revenues grew 8% year over year, results remain exposed to end-market swings in areas such as automotive and industrial. Management's second-quarter 2026 outlook of $300 million (+/- $10 million) implies only modest near-term growth.

news.Title: 記憶體爆關鍵轉折！分析師看好「漲停低價股」委屈了
news.Content:
台股今（3日）無畏日韓低迷走勢，逆勢上漲266點，記憶體族群再成盤面焦點，南亞科、華邦電及旺宏等指標股連續兩根漲停，分析師林漢偉認為，記憶體族群明天（4日）將迎來關鍵轉折，真正強的股票震盪完之後會繼續往上攻高，有些只是短暫跌深反彈，走勢出現分歧。

記憶體續強？關鍵指標曝光

林漢偉認為，從基本面來看，DRAM族群的延續性較佳，NAND Flash則會有一定震盪風險，如果投資人想要波段操作，DRAM相關廠商仍是首選，NAND Flash的廠商操作難度高，留意財報的效益。

林漢偉分析指出，由於美光上周大漲20%，禮拜五的三星SK海力士也漲了30%，因此台股的記憶體族群能夠連續拉出漲停，明天的記憶體就會有一定考驗，但就線型來看，華邦電已經回到半年線，南亞科也回到季線。

3檔被點名 記憶體8月仍有戲

展望後市，林漢偉認為，記憶體仍要回歸基本面，「7月加速趕底時，已經公布財報的股票逆勢走高，比大部分的記憶體更強，就模組廠而言，可以關注群聯與宜鼎，這兩家財報資優生還沒有公布財報。」

林漢偉進一步指出，「投資人想要搶跌深反彈或被低估的股票，就是要確認後面有利多，大部分的股票都會跟著基本面走，記憶體的利多在於每個月與每季的營收創新高，雖然會有反轉的時間點，但8月仍可以期待利多消息的反應。」

另外，林漢偉提到今飆出漲停的鈺創，「我們上禮拜有進去抄底，因為上個禮拜五公布財報，單季EPS高達4.81元，就算今年賺10元，股價80元的本益比才8倍，且鈺創還是IC設計，有記憶體、機器人甚至是AI眼鏡。」

林漢偉認為，鈺創的股價委屈了，投資人應該在8月選擇成長性好、本益比低且利多不斷的公司，從基本面著手，尋找股價遠低於公司價值的公司，在低點進場就能安心續抱。

news.Title: 華邦電利基型DRAM需求穩，接單/出貨續居高檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-08-03 10:10:22 數位內容中心 發佈

華邦電（2344）在產品面，市場討論焦點放在所屬的利基型DRAM區塊，尤其是與DDR4及中低階DDR5市場的連動。近期企業與工控應用仍大量使用DDR4，部分成本敏感產品對DDR5採用速度較慢，讓相關產品區間的交易熱度延續，華邦電的既有產品線因而受到更多關注。

另一個被反覆檢視的重點，則是華邦電在成熟型記憶體市場的位置。當前新增產能從建廠、設備導入到良率拉升，都還需要經過一段驗證時間，短期有效供給釋出有限，客戶端對既有供應來源的採購安排沒有明顯鬆動，華邦電現階段仍在既有產品與出貨基礎上承接需求。

從近期的營收表現來看，華邦電今年第2季營收已較第1季增加216.00億元，6月營收也較前月再增5.97億元，單月與單季同步墊高。上半年營收來到980.96億元，顯示公司近期接單與出貨金額維持在高檔區間。

這波營收擴大，與記憶體報價維持高檔直接相關。華邦電的產品銷售節奏，近期跟著價格環境同步墊高，單月、單季到上半年營收一路往上，讓公司在今年上半年的出貨金額明顯拉升，也把營運規模推到新水位。

news.Title: What a $10,000 Investment in Lam Research 10 Years Ago Would Be Worth Today
news.Content:
Lam Research (NASDAQ: LRCX) makes the machines chipmakers use to etch and deposit the microscopic layers of a semiconductor. It has never been a household name. But it got investors' attention on Thursday.

Shares of the semiconductor equipment specialist jumped 18% to about $298, the stock's biggest one-day gain since April 2025. The move followed record results for Lam's fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 (the three months ended June 28) and guidance for a much bigger quarter ahead.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

A pop like that is a good excuse to ask the long-term question precisely: What would a $10,000 investment in Lam Research made 10 years ago be worth today?

About $320,000, before counting dividends.

How $10,000 became $320,000

At the end of August 2016, Lam's split-adjusted share price was about $9.30. The same share fetches about $298 as of this writing, about 32 times as much. That's enough to turn $10,000 into roughly $320,000, before counting the dividends Lam has paid along the way.

With those payouts reinvested, the total climbs to about $365,000. And it's many times what the broad market returned over the same stretch.

The engine behind the return is the chip industry's growing appetite for manufacturing equipment, and the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out has lifted that appetite to record levels. In fiscal 2026, Lam's revenue grew 26% year over year to $23.2 billion, an acceleration from fiscal 2025's growth of about 24%. Net income rose 36% to about $7.3 billion, and earnings per share of $5.76 grew 39% from $4.15.

Showing how strong demand has become, Lam's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 30% year over year to $6.72 billion, up from $5.17 billion in the year-ago period. Earnings per share of $1.81 grew 34% year over year. Even more, the company's non-GAAP (adjusted) gross margin reached 52% of revenue in fiscal Q4, expanding from 49.9% in the March quarter.

"Lam delivered record revenue, operating margin and earnings per share in the June quarter as AI-driven demand continues to reshape the semiconductor industry," said CEO Tim Archer in the earnings release.

And management expects more. Guidance calls for September-quarter revenue of $8.1 billion, plus or minus $400 million, about 21% above fiscal Q4's record. Earnings per share are expected to be about $2.15 at the guidance midpoint, up from fiscal Q4's $1.81.

Story Continues

To put that guided quarter in perspective, it's more than double the roughly $3.7 billion Lam averaged per quarter in fiscal 2024, just two years ago.

It's worth noting, too, that Lam produces plenty of cash along the way. The company generated $1.46 billion of operating cash flow in fiscal Q4, comfortably covering the $325 million it paid in dividends and the $247 million it spent buying back stock. Lam also ended the quarter with $5.58 billion in cash and equivalents.

The next decade starts from a different price

Before extrapolating that 32-fold return forward, I'd remember what the ride looked like. Zoom out, and chip equipment spending is cyclical -- Lam's sales can still shrink when its customers pull back. As recently as fiscal 2024, revenue fell about 14% to $14.9 billion.

Today's buyer also starts from a very different price. Shares trade at about 52 times the $5.76 per share Lam earned in fiscal 2026. Even measured against the September quarter's guided earnings (an annualized rate of about $8.60 per share), the stock goes for about 35 times.

However, that forward figure assumes the boom keeps building. It's a premium price for a business whose sales fell by double digits as recently as two years ago.

Sure, AI-driven demand could keep equipment orders growing for years to come. But an investor buying now is paying up front for that outcome, in a record year, at a record margin.

So, would I put fresh money into Lam Research after a week like this? I don't think so. The stock may well keep running, and the business is arguably executing as well as it ever has. And I think shareholders who already own it have little reason to sell.

Ultimately, though, chasing a stock right after an 18% jump isn't something I'm comfortable doing, especially in a cyclical industry. I'd keep Lam on my watch list and wait for a better entry point.
